pr_title: Add etcd WithRequireLeader option to API watches
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Watches against etcd in the API server can hang forever if the etcd
cluster loses quorum, e.g. the majority of nodes crashes. This fix
improves responsiveness (detection and reaction time) of API server
watches against etcd in some rare (but still possible) edge cases so
that watches are terminated with `"etcdserver: no leader"
(ErrNoLeader)`.

Implementation behavior described by @jingyih:

```
The etcd server waits until it cannot find a leader for 3 election
timeouts to cancel existing streams. 3 is currently a hard coded
constant. The election timeout defaults to 1000ms.

If the cluster is healthy, when the leader is stopped, the leadership
transfer should be smooth. (leader transfers its leadership before
stopping). If leader is hard killed, other servers will take an election
timeout to realize leader lost and start campaign.
```

For further details, discussion and validation see
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89488#issuecomment-606491110
and https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/8980.

Signed-off-by: Michael Gasch <mgasch@vmware.com>

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #89488

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
"NONE"
```

/sig api-machinery

cc/ @dims @jingyih

issue_context.title: Clarification on watch when server (or store) is partitioned
issue_context.body:
After reading up on some corner cases with etcd client behavior (connections, streams, etc.) I came across the following option that has been introduced in etcd a while ago:

```go
// WithRequireLeader requires client requests to only succeed
// when the cluster has a leader.
func WithRequireLeader(ctx context.Context) context.Context {...}
```
[(Source)](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/67da93f739e33ee9b34792fccba2d0c100264ea4/clientv3/ctx.go#L28)

From the official etcd docs on client behavior:

> Client-side keepalive ping still does not reason about network partitions. Streaming request may get stuck with a partitioned node. Advanced health checking service need to be implemented to understand the cluster membership (see etcd#8673 for more detail).
Source: [clientv3-grpc1.23: Balancer Limitation](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.4.0/learning/design-client/)

I do not see this option being used in the API server when `Watch()` is [established](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go#L218).

Is there code in the API server that deals with these cases (etcd/API server node paritioned) and disconnects clients (REST, SDK) appropriately? Or are we at risk of having dangling (hanging) consumer-side client watches due to not using this option in the etcd client?

Related discussions:

[clientv3: clarify "WithRequireLeader" for network partition](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/9872)
[Network-partition aware health service](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/8673)

/sig api-machinery

cc/ @dims @jingyih @jpbetz @sttts
comments: @jpbetz was this something that was considered already?

We should be using `WithRequireLeader` for watches. (see also the [etcd Watcher godoc](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/3ac7a1151519af0816647d5f0757119c3f4a24ac/clientv3/watch.go#L65)).

It should just need to be added [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5d4553a90d110391d20324fe7f1890e48c8de659/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go#L214).

It would also be valuable to confirm that the behavior works as expected both when establishing watches and when a etcd member is partitioned after the watch has been established.
If anyone wants to own fixing this please self assign, else feel free to assign to me.

For this method:
```
func WithRequireLeader(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
```
It seems we should do:
```
diff --git a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go
index ca1583fb379..1bc841ca653 100644
--- a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go
+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go
@@ -126,7 +126,7 @@ func (w *watcher) createWatchChan(ctx context.Context, key string, rev int64, re
                // The filter doesn't filter out any object.
                wc.internalPred = storage.Everything
        }
-       wc.ctx, wc.cancel = context.WithCancel(ctx)
+       wc.ctx, wc.cancel = context.WithCancel(clientv3.WithRequireLeader(ctx))
        return wc
 }
```

Thanks! This is a good question. I am not exactly sure what is the semantics on kubernetes watch. It is correct that without `WithRequireLeader`, etcd server will not cancel watch stream when itself is isolated from the cluster. However, when this happens, other requests to etcd (including health checks on etcd) will fail. So the control plane is already in a bad state and is likely to be replaced / repaired either automatically or manually. IIUC, this means apiserver will restart, the its clients will restart their watches.
Oh I just saw Joe's earlier comment. If using `WithRequireLeader` aligns with k8s watch semantics, we should use it:)
@jingyih i'd support moving to 3.4.5 to pick this up!
@jpbetz I am happy to contribute but want to do some more testing and validation on the current behavior of `Watch` and with the proposed fix. Please give me some days.
@jpbetz @xiang90 @jingyih @gyuho Please see analysis above. should this work when the etcd + apiserver are on the same node or not?

Thanks for the careful analysis @embano1 

My take on this is:

For case **(2)** where the apiserver and etcd are co-located (and the apiserver only talks to that etcd), I don't see any reason why dropping the watch would help. In this type of setup, when etcd becomes partitioned, the co-located apiserver becomes unavailable and apiserver clients should route away from that apiserver entirely until the partition is healed. Even if the apiserver were to drop the watch, it is still unavailable.

For case **(3)** the behavior is already better than I expected. `WithRequireLeader` optimizes the case slightly by ensuring the initial watch connection is against a non-partitioned etcd, so it's still worth enabling, but not urgently needed since failover is already in place.

We should document in etcd that `WithRequireLeader` only applies to establishing the initial watch connection, the documentation is currently misleading.

> @jingyih you write:
It is correct that without WithRequireLeader, etcd server will not cancel watch stream when itself is isolated from the cluster

This is correct. ~~Please refer to the following test which verifies this behavior. The server should close the watch channel when itself is isolated from the cluster.~~ Edit: Sorry I missread the test.
https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/a04b74d4b4ebced2aca96dde08cb73b04bcdc484/clientv3/integration/watch_test.go#L789


> Looking at the definition of WithRequireLeader() it seems that this is performed only during establishing the Watch() but not reevaluated as long as the client has a successful connection to the etcd node (e.g. node is partitioned but not dead).

IIUC, this is not correct. After receiving the watch request with `WithRequireLeader`, etcd server will continue to monitor its leader for this watch stream. When there is leader lost observed for "maxNoLeaderCnt election timeouts", server will cancel the watch stream.
https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/a04b74d4b4ebced2aca96dde08cb73b04bcdc484/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/interceptor.go#L232

Thanks @jingyih, that means the documentation is correct then.

So while we haven't found any pressing issues that `WithRequireLeader` would fix, it does do what it should do, enabling it in the kube-apiserver won't make anything worse, and might make failover slightly faster?

> enabling it in the kube-apiserver won't make anything worse, and might make failover slightly faster?

Make sense to me.

BTW, I just did a quick test. 

1. start an etcd cluster of 3 members: A, B and C.
2. run `etcdctl watch foo --endpoints={endpoint of member A}`
3. stop member B and C
4. after some time, the etcdctl command prints `watch was canceled (etcdserver: no leader)`

Sorry for my delayed reply, wanted to do some more tests before replying.

@jingyih 

> BTW, I just did a quick test.

I can confirm this scenario. **However**, the tests that I did and which caught my attention because it was not what I expected from reading the doc string was to not shut down the peers but **isolate one peer**, i.e. simulate a partition which technically is also a "lost leader" scenario.

In this case I saw the watches not being closed (neither for `etcdctl` nor programmatically). Not sure if this is a bug or by design but I think it's more likely to have partitions than loosing the whole cluster where a majority of nodes is terminated/crashed (stop-failure). 

If you think it's worth and not expected behavior I am happy to open an issue in the etcd repo and provide more details. Even though [this comment](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/8673#issuecomment-398835414) in etcd makes it sound `WithRequireLeader` should address the partition scenario.

Note: I'm currently reviewing the network partition tests in etcd which state that the results I'm seeing are not expected. 

Update: looks like I'm experiencing what was reported a while ago in [this issue](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/8980) but it's unclear to me whether it's fixed, unfixable or what the workaround (from K8s perspective) would be.

@embano1 I'm in favor of you opening a new against etcd for the watch not being closed in the lost leader scenario (and linking to this discussion). If it turns out it is a duplicate we can always mark as such.
FYI. There was a bug in `WithRequireLeader`. The fix was backported to >= v3.3.19 and v3.4.5 https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/11687.

Thank you @gyuho and @jpbetz for your feedback.
After reviewing the docs and https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/8980 I think the issue with `Watch()` and how to deal with partitions is still open (see TODO below).

```go
// TODO(v3.4): configure watch retry policy, limit maximum retry number
// (see https://github.com/coreos/etcd/issues/8980)
```

The scenario where clients (Watchers or any client indirectly consuming from an etcd `Watch()`) would hang (forever?) is when the client gets partitioned with the corresponding partitioned etcd node **OR** when a whole zone/dc is partitioned. Since etcd picks safety (consistency) over liveness (availability) in this case at least not data corruption occurs but the overall system would be stuck when using watches instead of PUT/GET RPCs with timeouts. 

It would be ideal to throw a useful error, e.g. "lost leader", instead of hanging in "gRPC TRANSIENT_ERROR" state (which is what I'm seeing). Until this is resolved in etcd, perhaps the docs could be updated as `WithRequireLeader` is a bit misleading here.

I will comment on the etcd issue above and file a PR for the K8s watcher implementation to make use of `WithRequireLeader` as it is still a useful option when (re)establishing the stream. Depending on the environment, API server instances could have a health/liveness probe (or systemd equivalent) which could restart the process in case of a partition. Upon reconnect to the etcd node with the `WithRequireLeader` option it would immediately fail and error out accordingly.

review_comments:
I'm wondering what does it mean for leader reelections. Are we also going to break *all* watches?
Leader reelections may happen in perfectly healthy cluster (e.g. during rolling upgrade of masters), so I would like to ensure this is exactly what we want - what is the exact semantic of `WithRequireLeader`?

Another thing is that if this is infrequently changing resource type, it may trigger relists of all the watchers (even with watch-cache):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L422
[that can potentially overload and kill control plane]

It's not a newly added thing with this PR, but it may make it happen much more frequently....

> I'm wondering what does it mean for leader reelections. Are we also going to break all watches?

The etcd server waits until it cannot find a leader for 3 election timeouts to cancel existing streams. 3 is currently a hard coded constant. The election timeout defaults to 1000ms.

If the cluster is healthy, when the leader is stopped, the leadership transfer should be smooth. (leader transfers its leadership before stopping). If leader is hard killed, other servers will take an election timeout to realize leader lost and start campaign.

OK - that sounds fine from my perspective.

Though it would be useful to add this explanation in the comment. @embano1 - can you please add comment like what @jingyih wrote?
Updated the PR comment and the commit message with the explanation from @jingyih
Please add this comment to this file - it's much easier to understand it than look for the PR that added it.
@wojtek-t sorry, I misunderstood you then. With comment you mean in the code comment section (file) not the Github comment here, correct? Just wanted to clarify.

Yes - sorry for not being clear.
And thanks for adding.
